verdicts.strongest_argument: The underlying fact is published guidance and the interpretation is a published document, and the one option reading I am permitted on this name contradicts the conclusion. The 16-17% FY27 ARR and revenue framework was given by management at the 2026-05-26 release; the market's response is the largest reaction in the baseline history at -31.52%. Guidance that caused a 31% de-rating is not information the market has failed to absorb. The framing the finding presents as its edge - guide-floor binary, the invalidator being a reiteration with no upward qualifier - is not the hunter's construction either; it is quoted verbatim from docs/c93e70fe3290d74cd85541bdbc523d17e1e60435.txt, a post published at wp.optionbeast.com on 2026-08-29 and captured in snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 15, i.e. publicly on the web five days before the print. The finding even quotes that document making its central claim for it. Most importantly, this is one of only two names in this day's corpus where a genuine pre-print implied move survives, and it refutes the positioning argument. The same document records an implied move of about 13% quoted from Bloomberg, against a 9.79% historical median: the option market is pricing a move a third larger than history, which is the opposite of a market 'not positioned' for a bad outcome. A 13% straddle on a stock 47% below its 52-week high is a market braced for exactly the reiteration scenario the finding says is unanticipated. What is genuinely true here is that the 9.35% twenty-session rally raises the bar - but that is the run-up, it is in the baseline, and it is not an unpriced fact.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the entire thesis - the 16-17% framework as the single number, the guide-floor binary, the invalidator, and the observation that the 9.9% peer-driven rally means the stock already prices a constructive outcome.
'Zscaler Earnings: Sales Shakeup And Weak Guidance Overshadow AI Narrative' plus Evercore expecting a meaningful shift in the narrative - the May cause, published by a mainstream wire.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: A real pre-print implied move exists for this name - about 13%, quoted from Bloomberg in docs/c93e70fe3290d74cd85541bdbc523d17e1e60435.txt - against a baseline median reaction of 9.79%. The options are pricing 33% more than history, which is the market's own statement that it is not complacent. Tape: spot 177.80, run_up_20d +9.35%, run_up_5d -5.07%, pct_from_52w_high -47.13%, realised_vol_20d 61.8%. The 2026-05-26 reaction of -31.52% is in the baseline.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print datapoint on FY27 bookings or go-to-market attrition - a channel check, a partner survey, a disclosed sales-leadership change - that bears on whether 16-17% is a floor, rather than a restatement of the framework itself.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every peer print in the list was a major, separately reported market event, and the capture stores two independent write-ups of the pattern in the same sweep - the headline item at snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 24 and the optionbeast document, which records Palo Alto falling about 8% despite 34% growth and CrowdStrike falling roughly 4% in sympathy. The 'pattern is not aggregated' claim fails on its own evidence: two publishers in one capture aggregating the same set is aggregation. And the price has already answered it. Zscaler rallied 9.35% over the twenty sessions containing that peer reporting season - the market watched PANW get sold on 34% growth and bought Zscaler anyway, which is a considered response, not an oversight. The finding's own line, 'Zscaler's own tape moved the opposite way to the lesson', is the concession. The multiple argument that follows is the weakest part and the hunter says so: it cites a 'Cybersecurity Valuation Multiples 2026' piece in the same sweep and then admits no number was extracted from it, so the claim that Zscaler is the highest-multiple, slowest-guided name in the group is asserted rather than shown anywhere in this corpus.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: run_up_20d +9.35% spanning the peer reporting season, against run_up_5d -5.07% in the final week. The market absorbed the peer prints and bid the stock up, then trimmed into the event - both moves are in the sealed baseline. The ~13% implied move means any peer-derived multiple compression already sits inside the priced distribution.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The multiple comparison actually extracted - Zscaler's EV/sales or EV/ARR against PANW, CRWD and FTNT on comparable growth - which would turn the highest-multiple claim into a measurement.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a published options statistic drawn from a published document, and it is the sort of number that free earnings-option sites put on their landing page for every ticker. It comes from the same optionbeast post (line 454) as #0, which the hunter says should be collapsed into one cluster, and the finding is explicitly a magnitude observation with a two-sided tail and no directional content - the same statistic 'shows upside breaks too', as it says. The historical implied-versus-realised record for a liquid optionable name is exactly what marketchameleon, whose page is captured in the same sweep as item 24, exists to publish. There is also a partial internal answer to the finding: it argues that the ~13% implied and the 9.79% median both understate the distribution, but the 13% implied is already a third above the median, which is the option market having widened for precisely the reason the finding gives. Five breaks in eight is also not far from what one would expect when the implied move is a straddle-derived expectation rather than a bound.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the implied-move history - about 13% before 2026-05-26 against a 31%+ fall, 10.6% before the 2024 September print against a 20.6% fall, and five breaks in the last eight prints - and the ~13% implied for this print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Baseline history confirms the tail: -31.52%, -13.03%, -12.17% and +9.79% in the last seven, with a 9.79% median and 31.52% maximum. Against a captured implied move of about 13%, the option market sits between the median and the tail, which is a reasonable rather than a complacent premium.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Nothing; a published historical implied-versus-realised series is a description of the option market, not a fact it has missed.

interactions: #0 and #2 are the same document - the 2026-08-29 optionbeast post - and the hunter asks for them to be collapsed. #1's second corroborating source is that same document again, so all three findings on this name ultimately lean on one captured post plus one headline item, both from the 2026-09-02 15:46Z sweep. #2's implied-move statistic is also the evidence that most damages #0, because a ~13% implied against a 9.79% median shows the option market pricing above history rather than assuming a benign outcome.
